deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page develops a given power series f(q) into a continued fraction of the form f(q) = a_0 - q/(a_1 - q/(a_2 - ...)). In modern terms this is the 'corresponding' (C-, or regular Stieltjes-type) continued fraction, which is equivalent to the staircase of Padé approximants. Riemann works with the Taylor coefficients at q=0 of auxiliary 'remainder' functions. The left column (summation by parts) and the lower right column are attempts to get closed or recursive formulas for these coefficients. The mirror-written formulas in the left column are show-through from the verso, not part of this page (see transcription_corrections).

(A) MIDDLE COLUMN: SET-UP.
- The top of the column shows the target shape q/(a_1 - q/(a_2 - ...)) and the substitutions q/(a_0 - f(q)), then (a_0 - f)q/(a_1(a_0 - f) - q), and so on.
- Riemann tabulates partial numerators -q, -q, -q, partial denominators a_0, a_1, a_2, and the quantities 1, p_1, p_2.
- Definitions: p_0 = 1, p_1 = a_0 - f(q), p_2 = a_1 p_1 - q, and in general p_{n+1} = a_n p_n - q p_{n-1}.
- With r_n = p_n/p_{n-1}, the recurrence gives r_n = q/(a_n - r_{n+1}) [my restatement]. Since r_1 = a_0 - f, iterating gives a_0 - f = q/(a_1 - q/(a_2 - ...)).
- Requirement: every r_n = O(q), i.e. p_n vanishes to order n at q = 0.

(B) TAYLOR COEFFICIENTS OF THE p_n.
- Riemann differentiates the recurrence m times at q = 0, writing p^{(m)}_n for the m-th derivative at 0.
- By Leibniz, (q p)^{(m)}(0) = m p^{(m-1)}(0), so p^{(m)}_{n+1} = a_n p^{(m)}_n - m p^{(m-1)}_{n-1}.
- Conditions: p^{(m)}_n = 0 for m < n.
- Taking m = n in the recurrence for p_{n+1} gives a_n p^{(n)}_n = n p^{(n-1)}_{n-1}, i.e. a_n = n p^{(n-1)}_{n-1}/p^{(n)}_n. Riemann writes the case 'a_2 = 2 p^{(1)}_1/p^{(2)}_2' and the general lines p^{(n)}_n = a_{n-1}p^{(n)}_{n-1} - n p^{(n-1)}_{n-2}, etc.
- He iterates the recurrence twice: p^m_n = a_{n-1}a_{n-2}p^m_{n-2} - (a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}) m p^{m-1}_{n-3} + m(m-1)p^{m-2}_{n-4}.
- He normalises as p^m_{n+1}/(a_n a_{n-1}) = p^m_n/a_{n-1} - m p^{m-1}_{n-1}/(a_n a_{n-1}).
- The small table lists derivatives of p_0, p_1, p_2: p_1 has values f(0) - f(0) = 0 and -f'(0); p_2 has values 0, 0, f''/f'; and so on.

(C) RIGHT COLUMN: FIRST COEFFICIENTS.
- a_0 = f(0) and a_1 = -1/f'(0).
- a_2 = -2 f'(0)^2/f''(0), entered as 3f''_0/f_0-type entries in the table of derivatives of p_3, p_4.
- He then forms the products b_n = 1/(a_{n-1}a_n), i.e. the equivalence transformation to f = a_0(1 - b_1 q/(1 - b_2 q/(1 - b_3 q/ ...))). He lists:
  - 1/(a_0a_1) = -f'/f;
  - 1/(a_1a_2) = '-1/2 f''/f'';
  - 1/(a_2a_3) = '-1/3 f'''/f'' + f''/f''.

(D) NORMALISED RECURRENCE.
- Riemann puts p_n = q_n · a_{n-1}a_{n-2}...a_0 [reading uncertain] and b_n = 1/(a_n a_{n-1}).
- The recurrence becomes q_{n+1} = q_n - b_n q q_{n-1}. Hence q^{(m)}_{n+1} = q^{(m)}_n - m b_n q^{(m-1)}_{n-1}.
- The order condition gives b_n = q^{(n)}_n/(n q^{(n-1)}_{n-1}).
- Dividing by factorials, y^n_s := q_s^{(n)}/n! (the line 'q^{(n)} = n! y^n'). Then the recurrence reads y^n_s - y^n_{s-1} = -b_{s-2} y^{n-1}_{s-2} (Riemann's indexing).
- Telescoping gives y^n_m = y^n_1 - Σ_{s=1}^{m-2} b_s y^{n-1}_s, valid for n > 1.
- Initial data (with f(0) normalised to 1):
  - y^n_0 = 0 for n ≥ 1;
  - y^n_1 = -f^{(n)}(0)/n!;
  - y^n_2 = y^n_1 for n ≥ 2;
  - y^n_3 = y^n_2 - b·y^{n-1}_1;
  - b_2 y^0_0 = -f'(0);
  - b_3 = f''(0)/(2f'(0)) (Riemann's index).
- The final line y^n_1 - Σ_{s=1}^{n-1} b_s y^{n-1}_s = 0 is the condition y^n_{n+1} = 0. It determines b_n successively, in effect the Hankel/Padé linear system written as a recursion.

(E) LEFT COLUMN: TRYING TO SOLVE THE TELESCOPED SUM IN CLOSED FORM.
- Riemann applies Abel summation by parts to Σ b_s y^{n-1}_s. He introduces partial sums b'_s with b'_s - b'_{s-1} = b_s, b'_0 = 0.
- Substituting the recurrence for y^{n-1}_{s+1} - y^{n-1}_s lowers the upper index n by one per step:
  y^n_m = y^n_1 - b'_{m-2} y^{n-1}_1 - Σ_s (b'_s - b'_{m-2}) b_s y^{n-2}_s.
- Second partial sums b''_s with b''_s - b''_{s-1} = b'_s are introduced for the next iteration. A combination b'''_{s+1} - b'_{m-2}b'_s - b'''_{m-4} + b'_{m-2}b'_{m-4} appears.
- The line y^n_m = y^n_1 - b'_{m-2}y^{n-1}_1 + ... is the beginning of an expansion of y^n_m as a sum over iterated partial sums of the b's. In modern terms these are elementary-symmetric-type sums of non-adjacent b's, the standard formula for continuant coefficients. The derivation is left unfinished.
errors: The condition 'p^{(m)}_{n+1} = 0, m < n' should read p^{(m)}_n = 0 for m < n (equivalently p^{(m)}_{n+1} = 0 for m ≤ n). This is an index slip or misreading.

The written recurrence 'y^n_s - y^n_{s-1} = -b_{s-2}y^{n-1}_{s-2}' and the sums with limits (1, m-2) and (2, m-2) are not used with a consistent index shift on the b's. Different lines use b_{s-1} vs b_{s-2}, and b_2 vs b_3 for the same quantity f''/(2f').

The line 'y^n_3 = -f^{(n)}_0/n!(1 - 1/2 f''/f')' cannot be right as written. The correction term involves y^{n-1}_1 = -f^{(n-1)}(0)/(n-1)!, not f^{(n)}/n!. It should be y^n_3 = -f^{(n)}(0)/n! + b·f^{(n-1)}(0)/(n-1)!. It reduces to the written form only for special n or with f-normalisations not stated.
The summation-by-parts derivation in the left column is unfinished; the closed form is not reached.
The normalisation y^n_1 = -f^{(n)}(0)/n! tacitly assumes f(0) = 1 (otherwise it is -f^{(n)}(0)/(n! f(0))).

results.what: Recurrence p_{n+1} = a_n p_n - q p_{n-1} for the remainders of the continued fraction f = a_0 - q/(a_1 - q/(a_2 - ...)), with the order condition p_n = O(q^n)
results.modern_name: Three-term recurrence for continuants / tails of a C-fraction (corresponding continued fraction)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Wallis (continuant recurrences); C-fraction correspondence: Viskovatov 1805, Heine 1846-47, Frobenius 1881

results.what: Derivative recurrence p^{(m)}_{n+1}(0) = a_n p^{(m)}_n(0) - m p^{(m-1)}_{n-1}(0) and the formula a_n = n p^{(n-1)}_{n-1}(0)/p^{(n)}_n(0)
results.modern_name: Recursive (Viskovatov-type) algorithm for converting a power series into a continued fraction
results.usually_credited_to: Viskovatov (1805); later systematised in Rutishauser's qd-algorithm (1954)

results.what: Equivalence transformation b_n = 1/(a_{n-1}a_n), giving f = f(0)(1 - b_1 q/(1 - b_2 q/ ...)) with b_1 = -f'/f, b_2 = f''/(2f'), b_3 = f'''/(3f'') - f''/(2f')
results.modern_name: Regular C-fraction / Stieltjes-type fraction coefficients (first terms of the qd-scheme)
results.usually_credited_to: Stieltjes (1894), Rutishauser (1954) for qd; first coefficients classical

results.what: Telescoped coefficient recursion y^n_m = y^n_1 - Σ b_s y^{n-1}_s with y^n_{n+1} = 0 determining the b_n; attempt at a closed form by iterated Abel summation
results.modern_name: Linear (Hankel/Padé) system for C-fraction coefficients; expansion of continuants by non-adjacent products (Euler's continuant rule)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (continuants), Jacobi/Frobenius/Padé for the determinant formulation

results.what: (Show-through from verso) behaviour of the Laplacian under inversion v = r v', with factor r'^5

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's interest in continued-fraction expansions is documented: his posthumous fragment on the continued fraction for the quotient of two hypergeometric series (Werke) is a strongly asymptotic, Padé-type study. This page is a generic, classical-style computation of C-fraction coefficients from Taylor coefficients, with an unfinished attempt at a closed form. The recursive organisation anticipates in spirit the later qd-type bookkeeping, but nothing here goes beyond Viskovatov/Heine-era technique.

transcription_corrections: 'p^{(m)}_{n+1} = 0, m < n' is probably meant as p^{(m)}_n = 0 for m < n (or m ≤ n with index n+1).

'b_s = b'_{s+1} b'_s' (middle column) and 'b'_s = b'_{s+1} b_s' (left column) almost certainly contain a minus sign lost in transcription: b_s = b'_{s+1} - b'_s (or b'_s - b'_{s-1} = b_s as written on the neighbouring line).
'q^{n!} [?] = n! q^n' probably reads q^{(n)} = n! y^n, defining y^n_s as Taylor coefficients q_s^{(n)}/n!.
'p_n = q_2(a_{2-1}·a_{n-2}...' should be p_n = q_n (a_{n-1} a_{n-2} ... ), the normalisation of the p's.
In the derivative table '-2 f'''_0 f''_0/f(0)' is probably -2 f'''_0 f'_0/f''_0-type; the denominators are hard to read.
The mirror-written formulas in the left column (Laplacian under v = r v', the factor r'^5, dm = (r'/r)dm') are bleed-through from the verso, not content of this page.
Riemann's 'y^n_m = y^n_1 - b'_{m-2} y^{n-1}_1' line is a partial result (first two terms), not a final identity.
